text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Israel transfers close to 200 million shekels over two years to Tel Aviv bank account designated mainly for Palestinian Authority leader Yasser Arafat's discretionary spending.
- Israeli Treasury at loss to explain shortfall in internal revenue in August, says it was "totally unexpected".
- Chicago-based conglomerate Sara Lee in Migdal Haemek joint venture to make POY yarns.
- Telrad Telecommunications wins $15 million deal to provide switchboard equipment to Ghana's telephone firm.
- Museum Company, retail chain specialising in selling licensed reproductions of artworks, plans to open four stores in Israel.
- Attempts to set up meeting of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat stall.
- Netanyahu: There is no reason to fear Iraq conflict will affect Israel.
- Health Minister Tsahi Hanegbi appointed acting Israeli justice minister.
- Israeli Attorney-General Michael Ben-Yair threatens lawsuit against Bezeq Communications unless it cancels agreement signed with 17 Bezeq officials after company's formation in 1984.
- Israel takes unspecified "technical steps" to prevent element of surprise if Iraq launches Scud missiles at Israel.
- Haaretz military commentator Zeev Schiff: Slim chance Israel will be pulled into the confrontation with Iraq.
- Expulsion of foreign workers would cost 58 million shekels a year.
